title: Robustness of model-based control to digital-twin mismatch
research_question: How much of the joint controller's advantage survives when its digital twin is wrong, and do thermal limits still hold?
hypothesis: When the twin underestimates leakage or overestimates cold-plate performance, the joint controller exceeds the 80 C thermal target for some chip-seconds and loses part or all of its advantage over independent control; hardware protection still bounds temperature.
null_hypothesis: Joint retains its advantage and meets the thermal target under every mismatch.
independent_variables: twin-vs-truth mismatch (3 cases, each with a matched-truth reference)
baseline: same true plant with a correct twin
configuration: Mismatch applied only to the controller's model config (model_param_overrides).
evaluation_criteria: Within each truth case: joint vs independent paired difference with correct vs wrong twin; count chip-seconds over target.
known_limitations: Mismatches are single-parameter-group and static; real drift is gradual and correlated.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
